pr_title: Fix Blu-Ray menus after PR20260 - CDVDOverlayImage: cleanup
pr_body:
## Description
Fix Blu-Ray menus after PR20260 - CDVDOverlayImage: cleanup

Fixes https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/20544

## Motivation and context
Blu-Ray / Blu-Ray UHD menus are broken after https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/20260

This is not a revert of mentioned commit. This is an independent rework from a previous working version. Replaces alloc/calloc calls with vectors but avoids using additional vectors to move, copy, or transform data. That is, we try to optimize to the maximum without creating additional (unnecessary) copies of the data.

i.e. is much more efficient:

`uint32_t* rgba = reinterpret_cast<uint32_t*>(o->pixels.data());`

instead of:

`rgba = std::vector<uint32_t>(o->data.data(), o->data.data() + o->data.size());`


Also renames some variables to avoids confusing `data.data()`

Now is `overlay->pixels.data()`  and  `quads.texture.data()`


## How has this been tested?
Runtime tested Windows x64


## What is the effect on users?
Blu-Ray / Blu-Ray UHD menus are working again.

review_comments: Is there a reason you decided to invert this?
This seems odd. Is there a reason why you want to pass in an empty vector by reference rather than allocate the vector in the method and return it?
Isn't this a best practice to avoid copying the vector later when it already has elements? We seem do to this everywhere
I haven't looked deeply, but RVO - return value optimization - might be a reason to allocate the vector in the method and return it
As time go on, some compiler-specific optimizations do become guaranteed actually. I'm pretty sure that RVO is one of those and is now guaranteed
Did you mean to move this? It seems irrelevant?

All changes from PR20260 should not be interpreted as fixups or things that were wrong. I have started from the functional code in Matrix without looking much at the code of the previous PR (so as not to be influenced and make the same mistakes). So the resulting code has been different, which on the other hand is what is expected and what I intended.

Once this has been justified, effectively, the change is irrelevant and for this same reason it can also be left as it is.
and initialize with the definition. The cost of `= 0` is far less than the cost of a bug
